added_claim_errors: Quotes 16 CFR 700.10(c) as "if service is performed by anyone other than an authorized dealer"; the regulation's example reads "an authorized 'ABC' dealer". The words inside the quotation marks were changed, though the meaning holds (judged from my own knowledge of the regulation).
"Jiffy Lube shops have drained transmission fluid instead of engine oil on some cars": no source given, so this is unverifiable as a claim about that chain.

The email says flatly that "an oil change has no bearing on the transmission". That is an overstatement: if the shop serviced the wrong fluid, causation could be real, and the answer gives no support for the absolute claim.

Paraphrases Honda's warranty language as allowing maintenance "anywhere as long as it's the scheduled service and you keep records" with no link or booklet citation. It is consistent with the key, but the wording cannot be checked.

reasons: Both answers catch the false premise at the start and cite 15 U.S.C. 2302(c) and 16 CFR 700.10 correctly. A's email does more of what the key asks for. It says outright that the exclusion is wrong, asks for the causation evidence in writing (diagnosis and fluid analysis), and asks the dealer to submit a warranty claim. A discount comes up only as a fallback. A's escalation also covers more: Honda, then the state attorney general, plus attorney-fee shifting. B covers points A leaves out: Honda's booklet language, the 5-year/60,000-mile figures and keeping the receipts. But B's email only asks Honda "whether this qualifies" for coverage or goodwill, and "Either way... anything you can do on the $3,400" leans toward accepting the bill. Neither answer gives the Honda phone number, the National Center for Dispute Settlement or the FTC.
